mainTopic: The needle found in sacrificial meat: why the knife and hands stay pure, doubtful impurity in ירושלים, and doubts in the עזרה as a רשות הרבים.
overview: The גמרא continues with the case of a needle found in sacrificial meat, where the meat is impure but the knife and hands stay pure. It first asks why we don't learn that vessels, like hands, have no impurity in the מקדש. רב answers that the teaching about hands came before the decree on vessels. רבא rejects this, because both decrees were made on the same day. רבא then explains that the knife would be pure even with חולין, since nothing it touched can make it impure. To explain how the needle itself is impure, רב says it was a known טמא מת needle. רבי יוסי ברבי אבין says instead that the cow was muzzled and came from outside ירושלים. The גמרא then examines the dispute about doubtful spittle and vessels in ירושלים, and analyzes the משניות behind each view. Next it returns to רב's needle and asks why it does not make the hands and knife impure. רב אשי answers that the עזרה is a רשות הרבים, where a doubt about impurity is ruled pure. The גמרא challenges this with the rule of דבר שאין בו דעת לישאל and answers that this doubt came about through a person. It then begins quoting רבי יוחנן, whose statement continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why not derive a broad Temple rule for hands and vessels?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the needle case should teach that neither hands nor vessels become impure in the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And let us say: there is no impurity of hands and vessels in the Temple!
steps.whatsHappening: In the needle case, both the hands and the knife (a vessel) stay pure. So the גמרא asks why we don't state a broad rule that neither hands nor vessels become impure in the מקדש. This sets up the next step, which explains why only hands are mentioned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The known teaching says only 'אין טומאת ידים במקדש,' meaning there is no impurity of hands in the Temple. Yet the needle case shows the knife staying pure as well. The גמרא wants to know why the teaching leaves out vessels.

phrases.english: And let us say: that there is no impurity of hands
and vessels in the Temple!
phrases.notes: The needle case shows the knife (a vessel) staying pure too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the needle case quoted on the previous amud.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why is the Temple leniency stated only for hands and not also for vessels?

steps.title: The hands teaching came before the decree on vessels
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב (some say רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא) answers that the hands teaching was taught before the decree making vessels impure through liquids existed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב, and some say it was רבי יוסי son of רבי חנינא: 'Hands' was taught before the decree about vessels.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer explains why the teaching mentions only hands. When it was first taught, vessels could not yet become impure from impure liquids, so there was nothing to say about them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The impurity of vessels through liquids is a rabbinic decree (גזירה). If that decree did not exist yet, there was no point in saying 'vessels are pure in the מקדש.' So the teaching naturally spoke only about hands.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav,
and some say it was Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina:
'Hands' was taught before the decree about vessels.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Historical timing: the wording reflects the time before the vessel decree.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Leaving out vessels means vessels are treated differently in the מקדש.
steps.terutzMaskana: Vessels are left out only because their decree did not exist yet when the teaching was formulated.

steps.title: Both decrees were made on the same day
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects that the decrees on hands and on vessels were made on the same day, as the משנה lists them together.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: But weren't both decreed on the same day? As we learned in a mishna: the scroll, the hands, one who immersed that day, and foods and vessels that became impure through liquids.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks the timing answer. The משנה listing the eighteen decrees shows that the decree on hands and the decree on vessels were made together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 2 depends on hands coming before vessels. If both were enacted at the same moment, the teaching about hands could not have come first. So the answer collapses.

keyTerms.meaning: On that very day (the day the eighteen decrees were made)
One who immersed today and waits for nightfall to be fully pure

steps.confusionAlert: 'בו ביום' refers to one specific historic day when eighteen decrees were enacted together. It does not mean any random day.

phrases.english: Rava said: But weren't both of them
decreed on the same day?
As we learned in a mishna: the scroll, and the hands,
and one who immersed that day, and foods
and vessels that became impure through liquids!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: וְהָא תַּרְוַיְיהוּ בּוֹ בַּיּוֹם גָּזְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refutes the answer of step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the hands teaching came before the vessel decree.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה shows that both decrees were made together, so neither could have come first.

steps.title: רבא: the knife would be pure even with ordinary food
steps.stepSummary: רבא offers a new approach. The knife's purity is not a Temple leniency at all, since it would not become impure even with חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: Leave aside the impurity of the knife, since even with non-sacred food it would not become impure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא drops the earlier approach and answers the question of step 1 in a new way. He will prove his claim in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question in step 1 assumed the knife stayed pure because of a special Temple rule. רבא says the knife proves nothing about the מקדש, because it stays pure by ordinary impurity rules. So the teaching only needed to mention hands.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (signals a new answer replacing the old one)

steps.whyThisMatters: It changes the whole framing. The knife's purity comes from basic impurity rules, not from a special leniency of the מקדש.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
Leave aside the impurity of the knife,
since even with non-sacred food it also would not become impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of step 2 with a new answer to step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the case: the knife is pure for a basic reason.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The knife is pure because of a Temple leniency for vessels.
steps.terutzMaskana: The knife would be pure anywhere, so it teaches nothing about the מקדש.

steps.title: Nothing the knife touched can make it impure
steps.stepSummary: רבא proves his claim. The meat cannot make the knife impure, because food does not make a vessel impure. The needle cannot either, because a vessel does not make another vessel impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: This knife, what did it touch? If it touched the meat, food does not make a vessel impure. If it touched the needle, a vessel does not make a vessel impure!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא checks every possible source of impurity for the knife and shows that each one fails.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A vessel becomes impure only from a strong source of impurity. Impure food cannot pass impurity to a vessel. A vessel at this level of impurity cannot pass it to another vessel. So the knife stays pure even with חולין.

keyTerms.meaning: Food does not make a vessel impure
A vessel does not make another vessel impure

phrases.english: This knife, what did it touch?
If you say it touched the meat,
food does not make a vessel impure.
But if rather it touched the needle,
a vessel does not make a vessel impure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the claim made in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the knife would stay pure even with חולין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The basic impurity rules: food does not make a vessel impure, and a vessel does not make another vessel impure.

steps.title: How did the needle become impure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the impurity status of the needle itself is.
steps.simpleTranslation: This needle, what is its situation?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to the needle that made the meat impure and asks why it is impure at all. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The meat in the case was ruled impure, so the needle must carry some impurity. The גמרא wants to identify where that impurity comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: What is its situation? (literally, 'what is its doing?')

phrases.english: This needle, what is its situation?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the knife to the needle.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the source of the needle's impurity?

steps.title: A doubtful needle runs into the rule about doubts in Jerusalem
steps.stepSummary: If the needle is only doubtfully impure, there is a problem. Either רבי אלעזר or רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא holds that the רבנן did not decree impurity on doubtful vessels in ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we say it is a doubtful needle, wasn't it stated: רבי אלעזר and רבי יוסי son of רבי חנינא disagree. One said: they did not decree on doubtful spittle in Jerusalem. The other said: they did not decree on doubtful vessels in Jerusalem.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests the needle is impure only out of doubt, then challenges that idea using a dispute about doubtful impurity in ירושלים. The argument continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the opinion that doubtful vessels in ירושלים are not treated as impure, a stray needle found there should be pure. Then it could not make the meat impure. So the needle's impurity needs a different explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: A doubt (here, a case where we are unsure whether something is impure)
It was stated (introduces a dispute between אמוראים)

steps.confusionAlert: We are not told which רבי holds which view. 'חד אמר... וחד אמר' just means 'one said... and the other said.'

phrases.english: If we say it is a doubtful needle,
but wasn't it stated:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina disagree.
One said: They did not decree
on doubtful spittle that is in Jerusalem.
And the other said: They did not decree
on doubtful vessels that are in Jerusalem.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נֵימָא סְפֵק מַחַט, וְהָא אִיתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests a possible answer to step 6 and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the needle is impure only out of doubt.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By the opinion that the רבנן did not decree impurity on doubtful vessels in ירושלים, a doubtful needle there would be pure and could not make the meat impure.

steps.title: רב: The needle was definitely impure from a corpse
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that the case involves a needle that was certainly impure through a מת. Its owner lost it and then recognized it in the meat, so there is no doubt at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: The case is where someone lost a needle that was impure from a corpse, and he recognized it in the meat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the problem from Step 7. The needle is not a doubtful vessel. It is a known impure needle that its owner identified.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7's problem only applies if the needle is a doubt, because the רבנן did not decree on doubtful vessels in ירושלים. רב removes the doubt completely. The owner knew his needle was טמא מת, he lost it, and he recognized that exact needle in the meat. A certain impurity is not affected by the leniency for doubts.

keyTerms.meaning: Impure with corpse impurity (טומאת מת). A metal needle that touches it takes on the status of an אב הטומאה.
And he recognized it, meaning he identified it as his own
For example; introduces the specific case being described

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רב is disagreeing with the rule that doubtful vessels in ירושלים are pure. He agrees with it. He is simply saying this needle was never a doubt in the first place.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן שֶׁאָבְדָה לוֹ מַחַט טְמֵא מֵת,
phrases.english: For example, where he lost a needle that was impure from a corpse,
phrases.notes: A metal vessel that touches corpse impurity takes on that same severe level of impurity.

phrases.english: and he recognized it in the meat.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּגוֹן שֶׁאָבְדָה לוֹ מַחַט טְמֵא מֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the difficulty of Step 7 by defining the needle as certainly impure.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (אוקימתא) so that no doubt exists
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The needle was a doubtfully impure vessel, so the leniency for doubtful vessels in ירושלים should make it pure.
steps.terutzMaskana: The needle was certainly טמא מת, because its owner recognized it, so the leniency for doubts does not apply.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: The cow was muzzled and came from outside Jerusalem
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי אבין gives another answer. The animal was muzzled on its way into ירושלים, so it must have swallowed the needle outside the city, where doubtful vessels are treated as impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי אבין said: The case is where the cow was muzzled and came from outside ירושלים.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא answers the same problem in a different way. The doubt about the needle belongs to the area outside ירושלים, not to the city itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike רב, this answer accepts that the needle's status is a doubt. The leniency only covers doubts that arise inside ירושלים. The cow was muzzled the whole way in, so it could not have swallowed the needle inside the city. The needle therefore came from outside, where doubtful vessels are considered impure.

keyTerms.meaning: Muzzled, so the animal cannot eat

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Avin, said:
For example, where the cow was muzzled,
and it came from outside Jerusalem.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different resolution from רב's answer in Step 8 to the same difficulty.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case by where it happened: the doubt arose outside the area of the leniency
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The needle is a doubtful vessel in ירושלים, so it should be pure.
steps.terutzMaskana: The needle was swallowed outside ירושלים, and doubtful vessels from there are considered impure.

steps.title: The dispute itself: spittle or vessels in Jerusalem
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the dispute it mentioned earlier. One אמורא says the רבנן did not decree on doubtful spittle in ירושלים, and the other says they did not decree on doubtful vessels in ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now to the matter itself. רבי אלעזר and רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא disagree. One says: The רבנן did not decree impurity on doubtful spittle in ירושלים. The other says: They did not decree impurity on doubtful vessels in ירושלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The word גופא tells us that the גמרא is now studying, on its own terms, the dispute it quoted earlier. This step sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 7 this dispute was only used as a tool against the case of the needle. Now the גמרא examines the dispute itself. The two opinions differ on which kind of doubt the רבנן left pure in ירושלים: spittle, which might come from a זב, or vessels.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The matter itself': the גמרא returns to examine a statement it quoted earlier
Spittle, which is impure if it comes from a זב

phrases.english: The matter itself.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina:
One said: They did not decree
on doubtful spittle in Jerusalem,
and one said: They did not decree
on doubtful vessels in Jerusalem.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from the needle case to analyzing the dispute that was quoted in Step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The two אמוראים disagree on whether the רבנן's leniency for doubts in ירושלים applies to spittle or to vessels.

steps.title: Both rulings are already taught in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that both laws already appear in משניות, so it seems neither אמורא is adding anything new.
steps.simpleTranslation: We already learned the law of spittle, and we already learned the law of vessels!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges both opinions together. Why would an אמורא need to state something a משנה already teaches?
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אמורא's statement is expected to add something new. If a משנה already says these things are pure, both opinions look unnecessary. The next steps will show each source and then try to answer.

keyTerms.meaning: We have already learned it (in a משנה or ברייתא)

phrases.english: We already learned the law of spittle,
we already learned the law of vessels!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges both opinions from Step 10 as redundant.
steps.kashyaTarget: Both statements in the dispute between רבי אלעזר and רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Redundancy: an אמורא's statement should not simply repeat a law already stated in a משנה.

steps.title: The משנה source for spittle
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that all spittle found in ירושלים is pure except spittle found in the upper market.
steps.simpleTranslation: We already learned the law of spittle, as the משנה teaches: All spittle found in ירושלים is pure, except spittle found in the upper market!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the first half of its challenge by quoting the משנה about spittle. This makes the problem clear: the spittle rule is already written down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This משנה already says that doubtful spittle in ירושלים is pure. The only exception is the upper market, an area where non-Jews were often found. So the opinion that the רבנן did not decree on doubtful spittle seems to repeat the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
The upper market, an area that non-Jews often visited

phrases.english: We already learned the law of spittle, as we learned in a mishna:
All spittle found in Jerusalem is pure,
except for that of the upper market!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source text behind the spittle half of the challenge in Step 11.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the spittle opinion is redundant
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: כׇּל הָרוּקִּין הַנִּמְצָאִין בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם טְהוֹרִין

steps.title: The spittle rule applies even where a זב was known to be present
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the אמורא adds something new. Spittle in ירושלים is pure even where we know a זב was in the area.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the statement is still needed: it teaches that the spittle is pure even where there was a known זב in the area.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the spittle opinion. It shows that this opinion teaches more than the משנה does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From the משנה alone, we might think spittle is pure only when there is no particular reason to suspect a זב. The אמורא teaches that even when a זב is known to have been there, the רבנן still did not decree impurity on spittle in ירושלים. That added detail is why the statement is not redundant.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for this case; the statement is not redundant
That there is an established presumption
A man with a bodily discharge whose spittle is a source of impurity

phrases.english: No, it is necessary,
even where a zav is presumed to have been present.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, אַף עַל גַּב דְּאִיתַּחְזַק זָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the spittle half of the redundancy challenge from Steps 11 and 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: לָא צְרִיכָא: limiting the case so it adds something beyond the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The spittle opinion only repeats what the משנה already says.
steps.terutzMaskana: The opinion teaches that spittle in ירושלים is pure even where a זב is known to have been present.

steps.title: The משנה source for vessels
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about vessels found in ירושלים. Those found on the path down to the מקוה are impure, which implies that vessels found anywhere else are pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: We already learned the law of vessels, as the משנה teaches: All vessels found in ירושלים on the path going down to the place of immersion are impure. This implies that vessels found elsewhere are pure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now lays out the second half of its challenge: the vessels rule also seems to be in a משנה. The answer to this challenge comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Vessels on the path to the מקוה are probably on their way to be immersed, so they are presumed impure. The words הא דעלמא draw an inference: vessels found everywhere else in the city are pure. If so, the opinion that the רבנן did not decree on doubtful vessels seems to repeat the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: This implies that those found anywhere else...

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה does not say outright that other vessels are pure. The גמרא is drawing that conclusion from what the משנה implies (הא דעלמא).

phrases.english: We already learned the law of vessels, as we learned in a mishna:
All vessels found in Jerusalem,
on the path down to the place of immersion, are impure.
This implies that those found elsewhere are pure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the vessels half of the Step 11 challenge, now that the spittle half has been answered.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the vessels opinion is redundant
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: כׇּל הַכֵּלִים הַנִּמְצָאִים בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם דֶּרֶךְ יְרִידָה לְבֵית הַטְּבִילָה טְמֵאִין, together with the inference הָא דְּעָלְמָא טְהוֹרִין

steps.title: The second clause of the vessels משנה implies the opposite
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the inference from step 14. The משנה's second clause says vessels on the path up from the מקוה are pure, which suggests vessels everywhere else are impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: But by your reasoning, look at the end of the משנה: vessels found on the path up are pure. That implies vessels found anywhere else are impure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the inference it just drew from the first clause. It shows that the second clause, read the same way, gives the opposite result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 reasoned that 'only the path down is impure, so everywhere else is pure.' If we read the second clause with the same precision, we get 'only the path up is pure, so everywhere else is impure.' Both inferences cannot be true, so the method of inference itself is now in question.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning: turns someone's own logic against them
The latter clause of a משנה
The path going up from the מקוה

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the משנה rules that all other vessels are impure. It is showing that reading both clauses with precise inference produces a contradiction.

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning, say the latter clause:
On the path up, they are pure.
phrases.notes: Coming up from the מקוה, the vessels were presumably already immersed.

phrases.english: This implies that vessels everywhere else are impure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the inference drawn from the first clause in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference from the רישא that vessels found elsewhere in ירושלים are pure.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the רישא is read precisely, the סיפא must be read precisely too, and its implication contradicts the רישא's.

steps.title: The first clause is precise; the second only excludes the passageways
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the רישא is precise and the סיפא is not. The סיפא only comes to exclude the small passageways near the מקוה, where vessels stay impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the first clause is exact and the second clause is not exact. The second clause only comes to exclude the small passageways.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by deciding which clause we draw inferences from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the רישא is precise, the rule stands that doubtful vessels elsewhere in ירושלים are pure. The סיפא was written only to teach about the גזייתא, the small passageways where we cannot tell whether vessels were going to the מקוה or coming back. Those vessels were definitely impure before, so without proof of immersion they stay impure.

keyTerms.meaning: The first clause of a משנה
Precise; meant to be read exactly
Not precise; not meant for inference

steps.whatToRemember: Doubtful vessels in ירושלים are pure, because the רבנן did not decree there. The exceptions are the path down to the מקוה and the small side passages, where the vessels were known to be impure.
steps.whyThisMatters: This upholds the rule behind the second אמורא's view from step 10: the רבנן did not decree on doubtful vessels in ירושלים. But it also shows that a משנה already implies this rule. Unlike the spittle opinion in step 13, the גמרא gives no 'לא צריכא' answer for the vessels opinion here.

phrases.english: Rather: the first clause is precise,
and the latter clause is not precise.
And it comes to exclude the small passageways.
phrases.notes: There it is unclear which direction the vessels were going, so their known impurity remains.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: רֵישָׁא דַּוְקָא, וְסֵיפָא לָאו דַּוְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise reading of one clause only (רישא דוקא, סיפא לאו דוקא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both clauses must be read precisely, so they contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the רישא is precise. The סיפא excludes only the passageways, so doubtful vessels elsewhere in ירושלים are pure.

steps.title: Why don't the person and knife become impure from the needle?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to רב's case of a needle impure with טומאת מת found in the meat of a קרבן. A metal object touching a corpse takes on the corpse's level of impurity, so the needle should also make the person and vessels impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רב, the case is one where a person lost a needle that was impure from a corpse and then recognized it in the meat. Since the Master said that 'a sword is like the slain person,' the person and the vessels should also become impure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to an earlier discussion about a needle found in the meat of a קרבן and raises a difficulty with רב's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה ruled that the meat is impure but the knife and the hands are pure. רב explained that the needle had become impure through טומאת מת. Metal that touches a corpse, or something impure from a corpse, takes on that corpse impurity (חרב הרי הוא כחלל). A needle at that level should make people and vessels impure too, not only food, so why are the hands and knife pure?

keyTerms.meaning: Impure from contact with a corpse
A metal sword has the same impurity status as the corpse

steps.confusionAlert: This needle does not only make food impure. Because of חרב הרי הוא כחלל, it is strong enough to make people and vessels impure, and that is exactly why the question arises.

phrases.english: And according to Rav, who said:

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן שֶׁאָבְדָה לוֹ מַחַט טְמֵא מֵת
phrases.english: For example, where he lost a needle impure from a corpse
and he recognized it in the meat,
since the Master said:
'One slain by a sword': a sword is like the slain person,
then a person and vessels should also become impure!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַב דְּאָמַר: כְּגוֹן שֶׁאָבְדָה לוֹ מַחַט טְמֵא מֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the ירושלים discussion and returns to the earlier case of the needle found in the meat.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling, as רב explained it, that the knife and hands remain pure.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A metal needle impure from a corpse can make people and vessels impure, so the hands and knife that handled the meat should be impure as well.

steps.title: The עזרה counts as a public domain, so the doubt is pure
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the עזרה is treated as a רשות הרבים. It is only a doubt whether the hands or knife touched the needle, and a ספק טומאה in a רשות הרבים is pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: This teaches that the Temple courtyard is a public domain. So this is a doubt about impurity in a public domain, and any doubt about impurity in a public domain is treated as pure.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the question by explaining why the hands and knife stay pure, and he draws a new rule from the case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The meat definitely touched the needle, so it is impure. Whether the hands or the knife touched the needle is only a doubt. Because the עזרה is a רשות הרבים, the rule ספק טומאה ברשות הרבים ספיקו טהור applies, and they stay pure.

keyTerms.meaning: This teaches us (a new rule drawn from a case)

steps.whatToRemember: Meat that definitely touched the needle is impure. Hands and knives that only might have touched it are pure, because the עזרה is a רשות הרבים, where ספק טומאה is pure.
steps.whyThisMatters: It establishes that the עזרה is treated as a רשות הרבים for the laws of doubtful impurity.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:

phrases.aramaic: זֹאת אוֹמֶרֶת עֲזָרָה רְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים הִיא,
phrases.english: This teaches that the Temple courtyard is a public domain,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָוֵה לֵיהּ סְפֵק טוּמְאָה בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים.
phrases.english: so it is a case of doubtful impurity in a public domain.

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל סְפֵק טוּמְאָה בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים — סְפֵיקוֹ טָהוֹר.
phrases.english: And any doubtful impurity in a public domain is ruled pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: זֹאת אוֹמֶרֶת עֲזָרָה רְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing the case as a doubt in a רשות הרבים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The hands and knife should be impure from the needle.
steps.terutzMaskana: Contact with the hands and knife is only a doubt. Since the עזרה is a רשות הרבים, the doubt is pure, while the meat, which certainly touched the needle, is impure.

steps.title: Why the public-domain reason is needed if a needle cannot be asked
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from רב אשי that in a רשות היחיד the doubt would be impure. It then challenges this: a needle is a דבר שאין בו דעת לישאל, and such a doubt is pure in any domain.
steps.simpleTranslation: This implies that in a private domain the doubt would be impure. But this needle is an object that has no awareness to be asked. And for anything without awareness to be asked, whether in a public domain or a private domain, the doubt is pure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב אשי's answer from step 18. If the needle case is pure only because the עזרה counts as a רשות הרבים, then in a private place it would be impure. The גמרא points out that this cannot be right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known rule: when the thing involved in the doubt has no mind and cannot be questioned, the doubt is pure everywhere, even in a רשות היחיד. A needle has no mind. So רב אשי's reason of רשות הרבים looks unnecessary, because the case should be pure even without it.

keyTerms.meaning: A private domain. Normally a ספק טומאה there is ruled impure.
"Now consider" or "after all." It introduces a basic fact to build a challenge.
Something with no awareness to be asked. This is an object, animal, or person who cannot answer questions about what happened.

steps.confusionAlert: "דעת לישאל" is not about whether the person checking can be asked. It is about the thing involved in the doubt, here the needle. The question is whether it could ever answer "what happened?" A needle cannot.

phrases.aramaic: הָא בִּרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד — סְפֵיקוֹ טָמֵא הוּא.
phrases.english: This implies that in a private domain, its doubt is impure.
phrases.notes: An inference from רב אשי's reason of רשות הרבים.

phrases.english: Now consider: this needle

phrases.aramaic: דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ דַּעַת לִישָּׁאֵל הוּא.
phrases.english: is an item that has no awareness to be asked.
phrases.notes: An inanimate object cannot be questioned.

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ דַּעַת לִישָּׁאֵל,
phrases.english: And anything that has no awareness to be asked,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים בֵּין בִּרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד —
phrases.english: whether in a public domain or in a private domain,
its doubt is pure!
phrases.notes: So why was the reason of רשות הרבים needed?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא בִּרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד סְפֵיקוֹ טָמֵא הוּא מִכְּדֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning of רב אשי's answer in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's reason that the case is pure because the עזרה is a רשות הרבים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His reason implies the case would be impure in a רשות היחיד. But the rule of דבר שאין בו דעת לישאל makes it pure in every domain, so his reason appears unnecessary or wrong.

steps.title: The doubt came about through a person, so the needle rule does not apply
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this doubt is a ספק טומאה הבאה בידי אדם, since a person was holding the knife. It begins quoting רבי יוחנן's rule about such doubts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it is a doubt of impurity that came about through a person. And רבי יוחנן said: a doubt of impurity that comes about through a person...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the needle rule does not settle this case by itself. The possible contact between the knife and the needle happened through a person's hands. The גמרא starts quoting רבי יוחנן to back this up, and his statement continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The needle did not touch the knife on its own. A person, who does have awareness, was moving the knife. So this doubt is not treated as a plain case of an object that cannot be asked. Because of that, רב אשי really did need the reason of רשות הרבים to make the case pure.

keyTerms.meaning: A doubt about whether something became impure.
That comes about through a person's hands, meaning a person's action caused the possible contact.
A leading אמורא of ארץ ישראל. His principle is brought here as support.

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up an important limit on the rule of דבר שאין בו דעת לישאל. When a person's action is involved, the leniency for objects that cannot be asked no longer automatically applies.

phrases.english: Because it is a doubt of impurity
that comes about through a person,
phrases.notes: A person was holding the knife that may have touched the needle.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Yochanan said:
A doubt of impurity that comes about through a person
phrases.notes: The statement continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּהָוֵי סְפֵק טוּמְאָה הַבָּאָה בִּידֵי אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19 by showing that the needle rule does not cover this case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: the doubt involves a person's action, so it falls outside the plain rule of דבר שאין בו דעת לישאל.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the needle cannot be asked, the doubt should be pure in any domain, making the reason of רשות הרבים unnecessary.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because a person's hands were involved, this is a ספק טומאה הבאה בידי אדם. רבי יוחנן's rule covers such a doubt, so the reason of רשות הרבים is still needed.
